title: Branches as Expressions
goal: Use if as an expression that produces a value.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Morning: Control Flow Basics

sections.text: You use `if` expressions to choose a path based on a boolean condition.
`if` in Rust is an expression that yields a value. You can assign its result directly to a variable.

sections.caption: Both branches return a value to the binding.

sections.text: Because `if` produces a value, every branch must produce the exact same type.
Adding a semicolon to the last line inside a branch block changes its return type to `()`.
If branch types differ, the compiler stops with error `E0308`.
Matching on enums with `if let` is covered in the Pattern Matching deck later.

explanation: Use if as an expression that produces a value.
